study_design: Prospective cohort analysis using Cox proportional hazards models
reason: The study prospectively evaluates incident cancers and reports prostate cancer as an overall endpoint, without an aggressive, advanced, metastatic, or lethal prostate cancer analysis. The abstract gives only an approximate cohort size ('over 74 000'), so no exact analytic N is extracted.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: We prospectively investigated the associations between cigarette smoking, alcohol drinking, and the risk of twelve cancer types among over 74 000 low-income Black and White adults from the Southern Community Cohort Study in the United States.
estimate_classifications.reason: The alcohol row belongs to the prospective analysis of overall cancer-type incidence, including prostate cancer; no aggressive prostate cancer endpoint is established. The abstract does not provide an alcohol-specific prostate cancer effect estimate and confidence interval.
